s1.syndrome_frame: Multisystem disorder with musculoskeletal, ocular, and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Persistent back and bilateral hip pain
Increased range of motion in elbows, hips, and knees
Doughy skin with palpable bilateral piezogenic papules
High-arched palate with crowding
Left corneal clouding
key_facts: History of spine fusion at age 12 for cervical scoliosis
Hospitalization at age 2 for failure to thrive
Family history of maternal aunt with hemorrhagic stroke from cerebral aneurysm
Birth measurements: ninth percentile for weight, 58th percentile for length, and fourth percentile for head circumference
Septate uterus leading to hysterectomy at 42 years

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of hypermobile joints, skin hyperextensibility, and tissue fragility are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's tall stature, arm span-to-height ratio, and ocular findings such as moderate myopia are suggestive of this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's family history of cerebral aneurysm and her own findings of thoracolumbar spinal scoliosis and sacroiliac joint degeneration are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of skin hyperextensibility, joint hypermobility, and tissue fragility are consistent with this subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

shortlist.label: Kyphoscoliotic type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of spine fusion at age 12 for cervical scoliosis and current findings of thoracolumbar spinal scoliosis are suggestive of this subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including hypermobile joints (Beighton score: 8/9), skin features (doughy skin with palpable bilateral piezogenic papules), and history of cervical scoliosis and spinal issues, are consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome. Additionally, the patient's family history of a maternal aunt with a hemorrhagic stroke from a cerebral aneurysm could be related to the vascular complications seen in some types of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: While Marfan syndrome can also present with scoliosis and joint hypermobility, the patient's normal aortic measurements and lack of other characteristic Marfan features (e.g., aortic root dilatation, ectopia lentis) make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
rejected.why: Loeys-Dietz syndrome typically presents with more severe vascular and cardiovascular features, which are not prominent in this patient's history.

rejected.label: Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: While classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome shares some features with the patient's presentation, the specific subtype is not as clearly indicated by the provided information as the broader diagnosis of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

rejected.label: Kyphoscoliotic type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
rejected.why: This subtype is characterized by severe kyphoscoliosis and poor muscle tone, which are not the primary features in this patient's case.
